newsitem.title: POLAND: OPTIMUS SEES EARNINGS GROWTH RISING.
newsitem.headline: OPTIMUS SEES EARNINGS GROWTH RISING.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA expects its 1997 operating profit and sales to start growing again in March after they dropped in the first two months of the year, the firm's finance director said on Thursday.
The firm has said its operations were slowed in Janaury when it installed a new computer system, depressing sales by 10 percent and operationg profit by 31 percent.

"We expect March to be a better month than February...and to break even that month," Stefan Mroczek told a news conference, referring to Optimus' operating earnings and sales growth dynamic so far this year.
Optimus made an operating profit of 2.3 million zlotys over 1997's first two months on sales of 70.1 million zlotys versus 3.3 million zlotys on 77.9 million in the same period in 1996.
Net profit is up so far this year to 5.2 million zlotys from 1.8 million zlotys.
Mroczek said March's result would be helped by an expected dividend payout of about 8.5 million zlotys from its cash register subsidiary Optimus IC.

He reiterated the firm's expectation to lift net profit to 30 million zlotys from 16.5 million last year and for parent and consolidated earnings per share to be at 4.6 zlotys and 6.7 zlotys respectively.
Consolidated net profit would rise to 43.2 million zlotys from an estimated 25.9 million in 1996 on sales of 806.4 million versus 582.9 million respectively.
Mroczek also said the company was mulling a management stock option but not earlier than next year.
